articles.title: Wi-Fi 8 is appearing at CES before most of us have switched to Wi-Fi 7
articles.summary: Wi-Fi 8 devices made a surprise appearance at CES 2026, including a quirky new router and two new series of chips launching this year.
articles.body: The first Wi-Fi 8 routers and chips made a surprise appearance at CES 2026, and could launch this year, only a couple of years after Wi-Fi 7 debuted. So, if you don’t already have a Wi-Fi 7 router — and many of us don’t — you might want to consider holding off on upgrading. Rather than focusing on speed upgrades, Wi-Fi 8 promises improved stability. It offers the high speeds and bandwidth of Wi-Fi 7, but with improved power efficiency, higher throughput, and better peer-to-peer communication between devices. Wi-Fi 8 is also better at maintaining fast, stable connections when users are moving devices around, or moving them further away from their router. As a result, Wi-Fi 8 users will experience less “dropping out” or freezing and better streaming and gaming performance. If this week’s CES announcements are any indication, we’ll be able to try out Wi-Fi 8 for ourselves within the year. [Image: The mock up of the Asus ROG NeoCore Wi-Fi 8 router broke when Sean picked it up. Oops. Asus went from last year’s AI spider router covered in antennas to the ROG NeoCore, a Wi-Fi 8 concept router with no antennas at all. The polyhedral mock up The Verge’s Sean Hollister got a look at this week resembles a 20-sided die with a hollow bottom. According to Asus, the production model will offer the same data speeds as Wi-Fi 7, but with higher throughput and lower latency, so it can move more data with fewer bottlenecks and less lag. “The plastic mockup broke when I picked it up,” reported Hollister from the Asus booth. “Perfect,” responded Nilay Patel, Editor in Chief of The Verge. Broadcom also announced some Wi-Fi 8 gear at CES, including the BCM4918 APU and two new dual-band radios, the BCM6714 and BCM6719. All three devices are intended for powering residential Wi-Fi 8 routers and service provider gateways. Similarly, on Monday, MediaTek announced its family of Wi-Fi 8 chips, Filogic 8000, which it says will power “premium and flagship devices leveraging Wi-Fi 8 technology,” everything from enterprise access points to smartphones, laptops, TVs, and smart home devices. The first gear featuring a Filogic 8000 chip is expected to launch later this year. These new routers and chipsets are arriving only a few months after TP-Link demonstrated the first Wi-Fi 8 prototype connection in October. Despite brands going full steam ahead with Wi-Fi 8, the official IEEE 802.11bn specification hasn’t actually been finalized yet. The current IEEE timeline predicts that the Wi-Fi 8 standard won’t be ratified until mid to late 2028. Yet, Asus says its first Wi-Fi 8 routers are slated to launch this year. Early hardware would be based on a draft version of the spec, and would likely need a firmware update down the road to match up with the final specification. “What you are seeing at CES around Wi-Fi 8 reflects industry excitement for the next generation of Wi-Fi,” Kevin Robinson, CEO of the non-profit Wi-Fi Alliance, said in a statement to The Verge. “Wi-Fi Alliance is in the early stages of selecting Wi-Fi 8 features, and it is common for the Wi-Fi ecosystem to begin its work on silicon, reference designs, early product development, and technology previews ahead of Wi-Fi CERTIFIED availability.” Update, January 6th: Added comment from a Wi-Fi Alliance spokesperson.

articles.title: The Swan: Behind the Mirror Revisits the Rock Bottom of Reality TV—and Makeover Culture
articles.summary: Equally mesmerizing and appalling, The Swan kept turning up the dial until we gasped.
articles.body:
All products featured on Allure are independently selected by Allure editors. However, when you buy something through our retail links, Condé Nast may earn an affiliate commission.

There is a debate among scientists. Actually, more of a problem. How can we tell people of the future not to go into nuclear waste sites? How do we know our sign will last? How do we know that in the future people will be able to read English? Or read at all? What if they wander in 200,000 years from now and inadvertently wipe out their species?

The people in charge of the Waste Isolation Pilot Project settled on a warning that reads: "This place is not a place of honor. No highly esteemed deed is commemorated here… nothing valued is here. What is here was dangerous and repulsive to us. This message is a warning about danger."

So far anyway, that's the best we've got.

But nuclear waste won't be the only thing we leave behind. Future humans could unearth Rumi, Goethe, Bernini, Maya Angelou, Alexandre Dumas and think: Amazing. These people were beautiful, thoughtful, wondrous creatures, capable of depth and consciousness and profound beauty .

Or they could find a season of The Swan . And think: Well, that explains the warning.

We know a bit about what future people will think because a new documentary, The Swan: Behind the Mirror , turns us into the future people.

If you didn't watch The Swan when it aired in 2004, buckle up: This was a reality show in which a few dozen women were sent to Los Angeles to undergo…you name it. Facelifts , tummy tucks, nose jobs , whatever it's called when you take fat from here and inject it there, breast implants, intense exercise, calorie-restrictive diets, new hair, new teeth, new everything. They couldn't see their friends, family, or a reflective surface for three months.

In 2004, at the end of the show's first season, this publication called it the "surgical interpretation of Cinderella," which is definitely one way to describe cutting up a woman until the prince thinks she's cute.

"They weren't women whose faces and bodies had betrayed them. They were women whose faces and bodies had barely had time to form."

Yes, it sounds like madness now, but back then, people ate it up. If you were too young or too not-born to know it, some context: In the early 2000s, we were crazed for makeovers. This publication created an ongoing franchise called Total Makeover that lasted for years. The world was a makeover. We were making over women, men, little girls. We had gay men making over straight men–and would do so for a couple of decades. We made over brides. We made over bedrooms, living rooms, entire homes. You could not simply own a kitchen. Your kitchen had to have a journey. Nothing—not a human, not a cheese tray—was meeting its potential. We became so mad for makeovers that we created makeunders. Now we were trapped in a cycle of improve, reverse; do it all, take it all away. We were Goldilocks on Adderall. A zeitgeist in which "just right" could use some tinkering.

That was the world that spawned The Swan . And twenty plus years later, our world—the one that gave us #metoo, mermaid thighs , and body positivity—is the one that created The Swan: Behind The Mirror . It's a documentary of a reality show (wrap your head around that) that shows the other side—the one full of tears (not of happiness) and horror stories (one woman almost died in surgery).

First of all, the shots in the operating room make The Pitt look like an afternoon at Malibu Barbie's Beach House. But even more troublingly, there is the panel of, I guess "experts"? I'm going with "people." (One is a cosmetic dentist who has since had her license suspended.) They sit at a conference table cataloguing each woman's defects. One suffers from an affliction called "masculine teeth." Another could stand to "take some fat out of her face." A nose is "too long and too droopy." And then, remarkable for its bald villainy: "She doesn't have the greatest genetics."

In the world of The Swan , a 28-year-old needs a brow lift. Healthy teeth are ground down to nubs to make room for veneers . Almost no nose goes untouched. The mandate wasn't to make these women feel better. It was to find as many things wrong with them as possible.

And this is where the documentary starts to hurt. These women were young. Most were in their twenties; one was just 22. Some just had babies. They weren't women whose faces and bodies had betrayed them. They were women whose faces and bodies had barely had time to form. That was the saddest part: They didn't even know what they were going to look like when they grew up.

Almost without exception the women interviewed for the documentary talk about the low self-esteem they suffered from when they were young. Add to that a team of doctors, a mandate to change as much as possible as dramatically as possible, a network production budget, and the authority of prime time to confirm their worst fears: Yes. There is something wrong with you.

You have to tip your hat to the makers of the documentary for getting Dr. Randal Haworth to speak on camera. Looking back over his career, Haworth actually says, with words, out loud: "I've become more empathetic because I have a dog."

We are told by a former "Swan" that the producers did all they could to get "the money shot," that is, one of the women crying on camera. They found the deepest wound they could and rotated the blade. They asked one woman why she was unable to get pregnant. They pitted two sisters against each other. In one instance, and—you might want to sit down for this—the surgeons had found cancer in one of the women while operating on her, and the producers were reportedly "giddy." Cancer! Yay! Finally, some good news!

"Yes, these women volunteered for a makeover show. They did not volunteer to have their infertility discussed for B-roll."

Haworth, meanwhile, gives us his own philosophy: "There are no victims in life…only volunteers." Let's set aside the "volunteers" of disease, famine, war, and natural disaster for a minute. Yes, these women volunteered for a makeover show. They did not volunteer to have their infertility discussed for B-roll.

The Swan had to keep turning up the dial until we gasped. A makeover wasn't enough; it needed surgery. Surgery wasn't enough; it needed twelve procedures. Insecurity wasn't enough; it needed tears. The documentary claims the high moral ground but faces the same problem: It needs us to gasp.

You have to wonder if anyone caught the irony when they were making it. The documentary condemns The Swan for manufacturing reality, while offering its own more morally satisfying reality. And both want you to cry.

In the final scene of the documentary, we are brought into a Swan reunion. A lovely dinner party of former Swans, looking lovely and happy and healed. It's the end to a warts-and-all narrative but without any warts. Or at least warts that had been covered up by the flattering glow of dim lighting, flowers, champagne toasts, and laughter. The narrative is complete. The story is wrapped up.

Honestly, it could almost be a scene from The Swan .

articles.title: In 2019, Chip and Joanna Gaines bought Waco’s neglected Cottonland Castle; after years restoring the 6,176-sq-ft landmark, the ‘Fixer Upper’ property listed for $2.7 million has found a buyer
articles.summary: For years, Cottonland Castle stood as one of Waco's most intriguing landmarks, an imposing historic home that had plenty of character but needed someone
articles.body: For years, Cottonland Castle stood as one of Waco's most intriguing landmarks, an imposing historic home that had plenty of character but needed someone willing to take on the work. In 2019, that someone was Chip and Joanna Gaines. After years spent restoring and reimagining the property, the famous Waco couple's castle has now found a buyer, states an online report by PEOPLE. The Historic Waco Castle, also known as Cottonland Castle, went pending on Sept. 18 after being listed for $2.7 million in June. The eventual sale price has not been disclosed. The Gaineses had previously explored selling the property through an auction in 2023, adds the online report.A 135-year-old Waco landmarkAs per PEOPLE, the castle dates back roughly 135 years and occupies 6,176 square feet. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom residence combines the imposing character of a historic structure with the highly considered interiors associated with the Gaineses' Magnolia brand. Its restoration focused on preserving the property's historic identity while making the house functional as a modern home. Antique tile floors, diamond-paned windows and other period details remain central to the design, adds the report.Inside, the layout includes a formal dining room and a spacious great room, along with more distinctive spaces such as a card room, library and conservatory. Together, the rooms give the house a character that is unusual even among historic Texas properties, the online report elaborates.From neglected property to TV projectThe castle's transformation became a television project when the Gaineses documented the renovation for their 2022 Magnolia Network series Fixer Upper: The Castle.The show followed the couple as they tackled the challenges of bringing the aging structure back to life. For Chip Gaines, the property had long been a personal ambition. He had reportedly followed the castle for years, making repeated attempts to acquire it whenever it returned to the market. The restoration ultimately became one of the couple's most ambitious projects, combining architectural preservation with the layered design approach that has become synonymous with Fixer Upper.The latest property moveThe castle is not the only Waco property the Gaineses have been dealing with this year. Around the same time Cottonland Castle was listed, the couple also put their Colonial-style Hillcrest Estate on the market for $1.7 million. The five-bedroom, four-bathroom property had previously been offered as a short-term rental through Airbnb and the Magnolia website. It remains listed for sale, according to property records.The Gaineses have also taken on another notable restoration project involving an abandoned factory building that was transformed into the Gristmill. The property, which viewers may recognize from Joanna Gaines' Magnolia Table cooking show, was listed for $935,000 and remains on the market.A new chapter for the castleThe pending sale marks the latest chapter in Cottonland Castle's long history. What began as a neglected historic property became a high-profile restoration project and a television centerpiece before returning to the real estate market.With a buyer now lined up, the 135-year-old landmark is set to move into its next era, carrying with it the architectural details and history that made the Waco castle worth saving in the first place.Images Courtesy: EOnline and PeopleReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: How many Chromebooks will become Googlebooks before ChromeOS dies in 2034?
articles.summary:

articles.summary: We also spotted launch deals for The Witcher 3 Remastered, plus Fire TV Cube 4K and Fellow Stagg EKG discounts.
articles.body: Woot has the Razer DeathStalker V2 Pro TKL on sale for $130, a significant discount from its usual $219.99 price point. This keyboard is built for competitive gaming, with a low latency 2.4GHz wireless connection, and low-profile linear optical switches for faster activations that require a lighter touch than regular mechanical switches. The TKL layout cuts the numpad, but affords you more desk space for your mouse. [Product: Razer DeathStalker V2 Pro TKL | Razer claims the battery will last up to 200 hours with the RGB lighting off, or up to 50 hours with the lights at half brightness. If you’re interested in staying wired, or using the keyboard wirelessly with other devices, it has both USB-C and Bluetooth connectivity. You can also enable Snap Tap (Razer’s term for Simultaneous Opposing Cardinal Directions, or SOCD), which lets you quickly swap between two keys for strafing in first person shooters, for example, although it’s worth nothing that Valve has banned the tech in Counter-Strike 2. Other deals to consider * The remastered version of The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt just released, and a number of retailers are celebrating with discounts. While the list price is $49.99, PC gamers can grab the game for $24.99 at Steam, GOG, and Epic Games, with discounts available for the Xbox and PlayStation versions as well. The remastered version includes visual upgrades, tweaks to progression and skills, and both DLC entries: Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. * Best Buy has the third-generation Amazon Fire TV Cube discounted to $89.99, just over half off its usual price of $199.99. This square streamer supports 4K video with Dolby Vision and HDR, Dolby Atmos audio, and hands-free Alexa controls. With a processor that Amazon claims is twice as powerful as the Fire TV Stick 4K Max, it’s also a great option for Xbox Cloud Gaming. * Costco members can grab the Fellow Stagg EKG electric kettle for $99.99, a $30 discount from the usual price. I use this gooseneck kettle for my morning espresso, and I’m constantly impressed by its excellent temperature control and quick heating, and it adds a stylish touch to my coffee station.

articles.title: BMW’s revamped i3 boasts up to 468 miles of range
articles.summary: BMW announced new details about the upcoming i3 electric sedan, including battery capacity, range, and price.
articles.body: When BMW first announced it was reimagining the i3 as an all-electric four-door sedan built on its Neue Klasse platform, it left out a lot of important details, like battery capacity, range, and price. Today, the German automaker is finally starting to fill in the blanks on the i3. Let’s start with price. BMW says the 2027 i3 50 xDrive will start at $61,500, plus a $1,350 destination fee, putting it firmly in the Mercedes C-Class segment of competition. (Back in March, we could only guess a ballpark starting price around $60,000.) We also weren’t certain when the new EV would be available in the US; today, BMW confirmed an official launch in the first quarter of 2027. BMW also revealed new details about the i3’s motors. There are two of them — an electrically excited synchronous motor (EESM) in the rear axle that produces 322 horsepower and 321 lb-ft of torque; and an asynchronous motor in the front axle, putting out 165 hp and 188 lb-ft of torque — for a total output of 463 hp and 476 lb-ft of torque. The EESM, which serves as the primary drive axle, uses electricity instead of permanent magnets to power both its stator outer frame and rotor inner spinning part. An inverter acts as the brain of the system, converting direct current from the battery into alternating current for the motor, regulating the electromagnets, and monitoring performance to keep the motor running as efficiently as possible. The range figures quoted in the press release are pretty impressive. Back in March, we estimated around 440 miles of battery range, but BMW says the actual estimated figure will be closer to 468 miles, based on EPA testing. BMW may have caught wind of the 2027 Mercedes EQS’s crazy range estimate of 925km (575 miles) on the WLTP cycle (which tends to be around 10–20 percent more generous than the EPA’s estimates), and figured they could do nearly as well for way less money. Honestly, it’s a pretty decent bet. Frustratingly, BMW is still keeping mum on the i3’s battery capacity — though it does confirm that it features the automaker’s “Gen6” high-voltage battery built with cylindrical lithium-ion cells measuring 46 mm in diameter and 95 mm in height. The new cylindrical cells provide a 20 percent increase in energy density compared to the prismatic cells used in the Gen5 batteries. The BMW i3 has a few other tricks up its sleeve, including bidirectional charging with vehicle-to-load and vehicle-to-home capabilities, an intelligent charging flap that opens when a driver approaches a known charging point, and Plug & Charge for automatic charging at 10 different charging providers. The iDrive infotainment system represents a completely redesigned digital dashboard that replaces traditional gauge clusters with a heads-up style windshield projection. It stays visible even if you wear polarized sunglasses, and passengers can view or customize parts of it. The 17.9-inch central touchscreen presents as a free-cut display where you can drag and drop up to six “widgets” like media, weather, or navigation from the screen directly onto the windshield display. And the steering wheel uses “shy-tech” controls, in which buttons only light up when available and offer haptic feedback so you don’t have to look down while driving. In the vein of luxury automakers racing to cram more AI features into their vehicles, BMW is integrating Amazon’s Alexa into the i3. The much-delayed, large-language model version of Alexa can handle natural, conversational requests, search for online information, or manage climate and windows naturally. (BMW has been angling to get the new AI-powered version of Alexa in its cars since 2022, but was delayed by Amazon’s long development cycle.) When the car is parked, you can watch movies or live shows through the built-in Video app powered by TiVo (remember them?) and eventually Amazon Prime Video. The navigation system will run on BMW’s own maps, but with Google Places — points of interest powered by search data — integrated. The system runs on an Android-based platform and receives ongoing over-the-air software updates. But if you’re looking for more performance, BMW is also offering the i3 M60 xDrive, a high-powered racing variant with M-specific lights and graphics and 21-inch Style 1067M aerodynamic wheels. That version will arrive sometime in 2027 for an unspecified price.

articles.body: Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub will reportedly be revealed on October 13th. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that the smart home device will be revealed alongside a new HomePod mini and an upgraded Apple TV device. All three products are set to showcase Siri AI, Apple’s overhauled AI-powered assistant. The smart home hub, a new product category for Apple, will be the centerpiece. It will reportedly feature a 6-inch display which can be mounted on a wall or sit on a countertop. The hub is “about as thick as an iPhone,” according to Gurman, and has bezels similar to older iPads. It sounds like the hub will look a little similar to Apple’s iMac G4, thanks to a round, metal base that houses speakers, microphones, and a metal arm to hold the screen up. This also allows the display to tilt, and Apple will reportedly sell a second, wall-mounted version with a thinner base underneath for the speakers and microphones. Apple will reportedly use a USB-C power supply for its home hub, as the device doesn’t have a battery inside. Gurman reports that the hub will be available in “Apple’s standard gray aluminum finish.” It sounds like the new operating system built around Siri AI for the hub is going to lean into iPad-like apps, as Gurman reports that the Messages app has a two-panel layout. articles.title: Samsung’s new SmartTag is smaller, longer-lasting, and works with iPhones
articles.summary: The Samsung Galaxy SmartTag 3 Bluetooth tracker launches in the US in November for $29.99.
articles.body: Samsung has announced its third-generation Bluetooth tracker, the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It combines a smaller design and improved battery life with a few new tracking and software features, including cross-OS support intended to make it easier to share tracking information with friends and family. As revealed by leaks, the SmartTag 3 has adopted a squircle design, similar to the original SmartTag but with one key difference: There’s no cutout for a key ring. That means you’ll have to buy one of Samsung’s protective cases if you want to directly attach the tracker to keys or a carabiner. It has an IP67 rating for protection from the elements. The new design has benefits though. The SmartTag 3 is 35 percent smaller and 33 percent lighter than the SmartTag 2. It’s 10 percent more power-efficient too, stretching its replaceable CR2032 battery to 550 days of normal use, or 790 days in power-saving mode. While previous Galaxy SmartTags only worked with Samsung phones, the new generation has been broadened to support iOS too. Samsung doesn’t seem to expect it’s going to win over AirTag owners, but is instead pitching this as a way to share tracking information with friends, family, or dogwalkers for help with finding lost objects or pets. We’ve reached out to Samsung to confirm if other Android phones will be supported too. New notification alerts can be set to trigger when a SmartTag 3 moves in or out of a set area, movement detection alerts can trigger for smaller shifts, and location history helps you follow a tag’s movements. Tracking is handled by Samsung’s own Galaxy Find Network, rather than Google’s Find Hub, which launched following the release of the SmartTag 2. Once you’re within 200ft of the tracker, ultra-wideband (UWB) and Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding combine on supported phones for more precise detection. The SmartTag 3 is launching in black and white, starting in South Korea, where it goes on sale from October 7th. A US release will follow in early November, priced at $29.99 for a single tracker and $99.99 for a four-pack. That’s the same price as the SmartTag 2, and matches Apple’s latest AirTag and Google’s new Pixel Tag. Update, September 30th: Added US release date and price.

articles.title: Turn on lost-phone settings before you need them
articles.summary: Find My iPhone, Google Find Hub and Samsung Find have critical tracking settings to enable now, before your phone ever goes missing or stolen.
articles.body: You know that awful feeling when you reach for your phone and it is suddenly nowhere to be found. Maybe you left it at a restaurant. Maybe it slipped between the car seats. Or maybe somebody walked away with it. The worst time to start figuring out your phone's tracking features is after it disappears. Fortunately, iPhone, Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones include powerful tools that can help you locate a missing device and protect the information stored on it. Take a few minutes while your phone is still safely in your hand and make sure these settings are ready. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare. Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare With AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com. 8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT Turn on Find My iPhone in iOS 27 Apple's Find My system can help locate an iPhone when it is online. With the right settings enabled, supported iPhones can also remain findable when they are offline or for a period after they have been turned off. How to turn on Find My iPhone Find My network lets nearby Apple devices securely help locate your iPhone when it cannot connect to Wi-Fi or cellular service. On supported iPhones, Apple says the Find My network can locate the phone for up to 24 hours after it is turned off or up to five hours while it is in power reserve mode. Meanwhile, Send Last Location automatically sends your iPhone's location to Apple when its battery reaches a critically low level. That could give you one more place to check if the battery dies before you realize your phone is missing. Turn on Stolen Device Protection too While you are there, I would check another iPhone security feature called Stolen Device Protection . Open Settings > Face ID & Passcode and enter your passcode. Tap Stolen Device Protection, then make sure it is turned on. By default, Apple applies its added security requirements when your iPhone is away from familiar locations such as home or work. You can make those protections stronger by choosing Always under Require Security Delay. Stolen Device Protection can require Face ID or Touch ID for sensitive actions. Certain account changes can also trigger a one-hour Security Delay followed by another biometric check. Find My cannot be turned off while Stolen Device Protection is enabled. That extra hurdle can be especially useful if someone steals your iPhone and has also seen or learned your passcode. STOLEN IPHONES FUEL SCARY PASSCODE SCAM Google Pixel owners should check Find Hub Google now calls its lost-device service Find Hub. If you have added a Google Account to your Pixel, Find Hub is usually enabled automatically. Still, I would check these settings before you ever need them. How to check Find Hub on a Pixel For the broadest coverage, choose With network everywhere if that option appears on your Pixel. This lets nearby Android devices help locate your phone when it cannot connect normally. You should also open Settings > Location and make sure Use location is turned on. Google recommends setting a PIN, pattern or password too. A screen lock helps your Pixel use Find Hub's end-to-end encrypted offline-finding network. Supported newer Pixel phones can also remain findable through Find Hub for several hours after the battery runs out or the phone is powered off. For that feature to work, Bluetooth, Location and offline finding should be enabled before the phone shuts down. Check your Pixel's theft protections too Go to Settings > Security & privacy > Lost device protection. From there, review the additional theft safeguards available on your Pixel. Depending on your device and software version, you may see Theft Detection Lock, Offline Device Lock, Remote Lock and Identity Check. These features can automatically lock your phone in certain situations or require biometric authentication before sensitive account changes are made. Find Hub helps you locate the phone, while these additional protections can help secure it if someone takes it. Samsung Galaxy owners have two finding systems If you use a Samsung Galaxy phone, you can take advantage of both Google Find Hub and Samsung's own device-finding tools. How to turn on Samsung Lost device protection You will need a Samsung account on the phone to use Samsung Find and SmartThings Find. Send last location can preserve the phone's last known location. Offline finding lets nearby Galaxy devices help update the location when your phone cannot connect normally. Samsung says that if the phone is powered off, you may only see its last known location. That makes turning these protections on ahead of time especially useful. Check Google Find Hub on your Galaxy too I would keep Google Find Hub available on a Samsung phone as well. Samsung's current instructions say you can verify it by opening Settings > Google Services > Find Hub > tap on your device > Settings and checking that Allow device to be located is turned on. That gives Galaxy owners another way to locate or secure a missing phone through their Google Account. You may see slightly different wording depending on your Galaxy model, carrier or software version. Samsung notes that some menus can vary between devices. What to do when your phone actually disappears If an iPhone goes missing, open Find My on another Apple device or use Apple's Find Devices service through iCloud.com. From there, you can view the phone on a map, play a sound or mark it as lost. Google Pixel and other Android owners can open the Find Hub app on another Android device or use Google's Find Hub through a web browser. You can locate the phone, play a sound or mark it as lost. You can also erase the device remotely if recovery looks unlikely. Samsung Galaxy owners can use Samsung Find or SmartThings Find through their Samsung account in addition to Google Find Hub. If the phone appears to be sitting somewhere nearby, playing a sound can save you from tearing the house apart. However, if the map shows your phone somewhere unfamiliar and you suspect it was stolen, avoid trying to recover it yourself. Contact law enforcement instead. Watch out for scams after your phone is stolen Losing the phone can also open the door to another problem. Thieves have used convincing Apple-style texts and fake Find My websites to trick stolen iPhone owners into revealing their passcodes. A message may claim that your missing phone has suddenly been found and include a link where you can supposedly see its location. Avoid tapping those links. Instead, open Find My yourself or go directly to Apple's official Find Devices service. The same basic rule applies to Android. If a message claims your missing device has been located, open Google Find Hub or Samsung Find directly rather than signing in through a link somebody sent you. Pro tip: Use strong antivirus software. Strong security software can help warn you about malicious links, phishing sites and other online threats that may appear after your phone is stolen. It adds another layer of protection, but you should still avoid clicking unexpected messages claiming your missing phone has been found. Instead, open Find My, Google Find Hub or Samsung Find directly. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. A few minutes now can save a lot of panic later Most of us do not think much about these settings while our phone is sitting safely in our hand. Then the phone disappears and suddenly every one of them becomes very important. I would check them now. Make sure your phone can be located, make sure offline finding is enabled and confirm that you know which account you would need to sign in to from another device. You may never need any of these features. If you do, you will already know where to start. Kurt's key takeaways Your phone already has some impressive tools for finding it, but those tools work best when you prepare before the phone goes missing. On an iPhone, I would make sure Find My network and Send Last Location are enabled. Pixel owners should check Find Hub and offline finding, while Galaxy users can add Samsung's Lost device protection on top of Google's system. I would also spend another minute reviewing the theft protections available on your phone. Apple's Stolen Device Protection and Google's theft protection features can make it harder for someone who gets your phone to take control of your accounts. That extra layer could become incredibly valuable when you are already dealing with the stress of a missing device. articles.title: Potato by air
articles.summary: ﻿The day the dads in my neighborhood discovered drone delivery
articles.body: The Wing Hummingbird 7000W-B delivery drone weighs less than 15 pounds. It has 16 propellers — four for horizontal movement and 12 for vertical — a top speed of 60 miles per hour, a carrying capacity of up to 2.7 pounds, and a delivery radius of about six miles. It is authorized by the FAA for beyond-line-of-sight piloting. As a feat of engineering, it is impressive. So far I’ve mostly used it to send people potatoes. [Media: It all started a few Sunday mornings ago when my neighbor Will added me and a half dozen other local dads to a group chat. I only recognized a few of the numbers. “Anyone looking for dumb stuff to entertain the kids?” he wrote, under a video of a drone lowering a blue doggie bag into his backyard. He’d discovered that we were now in the delivery range for drone service Wing’s partnership with Walmart, and could get household items dropped onto our lawns in 25 minutes. “Hopefully liquor store will get on board soon.” Ever since I saw the video of an Amazon drone dropping a package in someone’s pool, I’ve needed to know one thing: Do you have to order drone delivery to your own yard? I raised the question in the chat. [Image: Turns out: no and yes. Will, a few minutes later: “Nathan I just ordered you a potato to see if I can send to other people. 8 minutes out.” Two minutes after that, a neighbor named Rick: “Will just want you to know you’re going to get your potato first.” Rick and Will had each scanned the list of deliverable items — over two thousand of them — and independently arrived at the same conclusion. “There is currently an air strike squadron of potatoes headed to our neighborhood,” Rick wrote. [Image: It’s a bird! It’s a plane! It’s a cropped still from a video! At 12:14PM, a drone dropped a doggie bag in my yard. It contained a single russet potato and a bottle of water. Three minutes later, another arrived in Will’s yard, also containing a single potato and a bottle of water. (The water bottle seems to have been added as ballast; every Wing order I’ve placed came with one.) Someone posted “The drones are everywhere.” Those of us who hadn’t met introduced ourselves. An apparently more practical dad named Jason ordered himself a pair of gloves. Dev, who lives in the next development over, was just out of drone range and could only watch in envy. Eventually, a storm rolled in and the potato drones tapered off. [Image: [Image: My sixth-grader turned our sky potato into oven fries; Will baked his. The wild thing — aside from the fact that you can just order a drone delivery to someone else’s yard — is that each potato delivery cost 82 cents. Total. Each order came from the Walmart Supercenter a few miles away. Wing is absolutely losing money on this. There’s no minimum order, there’s no delivery fee, and the prices are the same as in-store. Wing’s not even collecting sales tax. Welcome back, millennial lifestyle subsidy! At these prices, if you’re not using drones to send potatoes to your neighbors you’re leaving money on the table. That evening, I remembered that my friend Bill had been going through a rough time lately. I sent him a potato. Okay, technically, Wing’s terms of service state “You will not use the Service to engage in any unlawful behavior, or to cause harassment, nuisance, annoyance or inconvenience to Wing, its users or any other person.” And I can definitely see ways you could abuse the system to do that. While I lacked actual permission to land a drone potato in Bill’s yard, based on our relationship, I was confident I had spiritual permission. (This was confirmed a couple of days later when he asked me to drone deliver some candy for his kids. I sent the candy, and then another potato, and then the link to the Wing app.) So what’s stopping someone from using this to harass people, beyond your own moral compass and the fact that they ask you not to? When I asked what safeguards the company had in place to prevent unauthorized deliveries, Wing spokesperson Jessie Poole-Strang wrote: > Wing has safely completed over 1 million residential drone deliveries, averaging thousands per day. Customers must be physically present for their first order, and every order requires a verified account and confirmation of a clear delivery zone. Just like traditional delivery or mailing a package, customers can choose to send an order to a friend or family member’s address that lives in eligible service areas. In the rare event a resident ever has a concern about a delivery to their property, our support team can help (support@wing.com). Now, is drone delivery wasteful? If you’re only buying a single lightweight item — like a stick of deodorant, a bottle of sunscreen, or a potato — it seems more environmentally friendly than driving to the store. And as long as it’s subsidized, it’s way cheaper than DoorDash or whatever people use. I could see situations where it would be genuinely useful, especially if you can’t leave the house but you desperately need a bottle of ibuprofen and a Gatorade (for example). And of course it would be preposterous to DoorDash someone a single raw potato. [Image: Would you? Of course, once you order more than a pound or so of stuff, that math goes off the rails. One afternoon, my wife ordered a box of frozen horchata mochi and a pint of gelato — among the few frozen desserts on the list. They arrived in two separate drones, three minutes apart, and each came with a small bottle of water. They held up surprisingly well during their 7-minute trips in the full Texas sun, considering the total lack of insulation. But it did feel silly to get two drones for two items. That’s how they get you, of course. They hook you with convenience while hiding the true cost of the service. Drone delivery further squeezes gig workers in an already shrinking labor market, and it’s one more excuse for big companies to suppress wages. You don’t have to pay a drone, and you don’t have to tip it, either. It’s been just over three weeks since we found out we had access to subsidized drone delivery. Aside from the two desserts and a couple of bags of gummy Nerds clusters, I’ve only used it to send potatoes to the dads. I sent three last week, plus one to myself to throw them off the scent. I’ve probably blown my cover now. The other day someone — not me — escalated and sent Rick a broccoli potato soup. I’m pretty sure it was Will. What have I learned from all of this? Well, I now know a few more people in my neighborhood. I’ve learned that drone delivery is way more useful to me than agentic AI has ever been. And that given the opportunity to airdrop subsidized potatoes to my friends, I’ll take it.

articles.title: Amazon's new Fire TV Stick 4K comes with an actually good remote | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon’s new Fire TV Stick 4K is slimmer and faster, but its biggest upgrade may be the thing you’ll actually hold in your hand: a redesigned remote that’s easier to use, especially in the dark.
articles.body:
As part of its fall hardware refresh, Amazon on Wednesday introduced the next version of its Fire TV Stick 4K , which is now slimmer and faster and can be directly charged via a TV’s USB port.

But the real news is that the device comes with an actually good remote control. No more blue Alexa button and a home button you can feel in the dark, a button for adding favorites, and a new shape that makes it more comfortable to hold in the hand.

It may seem funny that a remote control is the best part about the new streamer, which Amazon claims is 20% to 40% faster than leading competitors. But true TV connoisseurs know that a bad remote can ruin what would otherwise be a great watching experience. Amazon’s older voice remote wasn’t terrible, but it had plenty of room for improvement.

The new one features a different shape and curvature that make it easy to hold and point at the TV. Its buttons and layout have also been redesigned with an eye toward how people often use their remote controls: in a dark room.

If you’ve spent any time with remote controls, you know that you can sometimes struggle to find and mash the right button when you can’t see the device well, especially if the icons on the buttons don’t make much sense.

That was the case with the older remote, which featured a prominent, blue Alexa voice button at the top center. That button has now been replaced with a more subtle black microphone button at the top right, which also has a slight dish at the top, so you can find it by feel.

The new remote’s home button can also be found with touch only, as it has a metallic finish (and an orangish-reddish hue) that makes it feel distinct. The power button at the top left is recessed, which helps you avoid accidentally turning off the device, and the D-pad is flatter, which makes it easier to roll your thumb around. Lastly, the center of the D-pad now has a more tactile click.

And, in response to user feedback, there’s finally a Favorites button you can program to launch a preferred app or even enable an oft-used option, like toggling Closed Captions or Dialog Boost.

The new remote control will come with the Fire TV Stick 4K but is also being sold separately for those who just want an upgrade.

The 4K Stick itself has 8GB of internal storage, a quad-core 1.7 GHz processor, and support for Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, and Bluetooth Low Energy. It also supports HDR10, HDR10+, HLG, H.265, H.264, VP9, and AV1 video formats, and can output at 2160 p, 1080 p, and 720 p resolutions at up to 60 frames per second.

The 4K Stick joins the full lineup, which also includes an HD Stick, a 4K “Max” Stick (faster, more storage), and the Fire TV Cube.

The Fire TV 4K Stick is priced at $59.99 but will launch at a discounted price of $29.99. It’s initially available in the U.S., Canada, Japan, Mexico, United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Australia, and New Zealand.

The remote will ship in late October and costs $14.99 in the U.S.

articles.title: Google launches Fitbit Air in India, though its high price might deter the masses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Fitbit Air costs around $146 in India, roughly $47 more than its U.S. pricing.
articles.body:
Google on Wednesday launched the screen-less Fitbit Air fitness tracker in India, but is pricing it at ₹13,999 (roughly $146), ostensibly positioning it as a premium device. Comparatively, the device costs $99 in the U.S.

Unveiled in May , the Fitbit Air features health and fitness tracking, like 24/7 heart rate monitoring, heart rhythm monitoring with A-fib (atrial fibrillation) alerts, blood oxygen level, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, sleep stages, and duration.

The device’s screen-less form is a bid to tap into the growing popularity of screen-less devices as people shy away from screens, opting for distraction-free health gadgets like Whoop’s fitness bands and Oura’s rings — though the new Fitbit is more pocket-friendly.

The health tracking space now has screen-less devices from Garmin , Fitbit founders’ new company, Luffu Link , as well as from Indian startups like Noise and Urban , which have been trying to undercut their Western rivals on price.

Research firm IDC noted in its global wearables report that despite a declining number of wristband shipments, screen-less trackers are carving out a niche. India currently accounts for only 5% of the screenless wearable market, per Counterpoint Research , and a wearable priced like a premium device might not make a dent in overall numbers, despite having a big name like Fitbit or Google behind it.

The Fitbit Air is available for purchase on the Google Store and retail partners, including Flipkart, Croma, Reliance Digital, and Vijay Sales, from October 2. Google is also offering a free, three-month Google Health premium membership with the new band.

articles.title: The Halide camera app now offers full control of the iPhone 18 Pro’s aperture
articles.summary: Today’s update to the Halide Mark III camera lets you dial in any aperture setting when shooting with the iPhone 18 Pro.
articles.body: A new update to Lux Optics’ anti-algorithm Halide camera app for the iPhone and iPad adds two new photography looks and support for the variable aperture on the new iPhone 18 Pro’s main camera. Halide isn’t the first alternative to the native iOS camera app to add support for the new feature, but it offers more finite control over aperture settings than other third-party apps. The iOS camera app limits aperture adjustments to just four presets, but both the BlackMagic Camera and Moment Pro Camera II apps expand that to 10 presets in 1/3 stop increments, similar to what most digital cameras offer. Halide Mark III goes even further by letting you select any f-stop setting from f/1.48 down to f/4.0. Although it’s hard to imagine you’ll see any noticeable difference between f/4.0 and f/3.99, the option is available. The Halide developers are also considering adding f-stop presets in future updates based on user feedback. [Image: The new Dawn look (left) adds warmth to images while Quicksilver (right) mutes colors and boosts contrast. articles.title: Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
articles.summary: Reddit is going to limit access to “Old Reddit” to logged-in accounts who have used the experience in six months from when the change rolls out as part of its efforts to combat scraping and automated traffic.
articles.body: Reddit is further limiting who can use the “Old Reddit” experience as part of its efforts to combat scraping and automated traffic. Reddit recently started forcing users to log in to be able to use Old Reddit, but in the “next few months,” the company says that you’ll have to be logged in and have used Old Reddit within the last six months from when the change rolls out to be able to continue browsing the platform with the classic experience. Reddit says the six-month window covers “the vast majority of all Old Reddit users.” The announcement didn’t go into detail, but it’s clearly aimed at blocking not just new account creation for bots, but also any bots that might access unused or abandoned accounts. As part of the changes, Reddit will stop supporting RSS feeds on November 13th because RSS is “now a common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse,” and suggested replacements like Discord Relay for moderation help. Reddit: > If you use RSS for feeds outside of a community you moderate, there is no replacement. We know RSS has been a beloved part of the open web for a long time, and we’re grateful to everyone who used it to stay connected to Reddit. The company has been waging war against unsanctioned access to its data for some time, including blocking the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine to prevent AI scraping, suing Anthropic over alleged unauthorized bot access, and striking deals with Google and OpenAI to use Reddit data for training. Reddit knows that Old Reddit is beloved by many users, and in May 2025, CEO Steve Huffman said the company would “keep it online as long as people are using it.” But this past August, Huffman said that Reddit had gotten to a point where “we need to make some changes” because the experience was being used by “everyone who spams, scrapes, or does anything bad on Reddit.” In its announcement today, Reddit said that the recent login requirement for Old Reddit “helped reduce scraping and automated abuse” but “still allowed any logged-in account to access Old Reddit, including accounts with no prior Old Reddit use.” Logged-in moderators, however, will still be able to use Old Reddit without a recent usage requirement. Reddit also shared updates for the previously announced transition moving apps and bots that use Reddit’s public data API to the company’s developer platform. Reddit will begin removing API access for users that haven’t registered their apps by January 12th, 2027, and all remaining public API access “will end in March 2027.”

articles.title: Bigg Boss 20: Kanika Mann slams Qazi Touqeer over his 'Lollipop and biology' joke: says 'It’s cheap, tumhe main tameez sikhake jaungi'
articles.summary: The latest episode of Bigg Boss 20 witnessed an argument between Qazi Touqeer and Kanika Mann.
articles.body: The latest episode of Bigg Boss 20 witnessed an argument between Qazi Touqeer and Kanika Mann. The duo once again got into a verbal fight after a conversation between them took an uncomfortable turn.During a recent interaction, Qazi once again made a lollipop-related joke that did not sit well with Kanika. For those unaware, Kanika had earlier objected to the same joke and remarks being used around her.Kanika, who is known for voicing out her opinion, had clearly mentioned about maintaining boundaries. She immediately confronted Qazi over his Lollipop comment and walked out of the conversation. She called him out for his remark and made it clear that she did not find the joke funny and instead considered it cheap.That was cheap, Qazi Touqeer. I don’t expect cheap things from you. Tameez sikhaake jaungi. It’s cheap,” Kanika told Qazi, making her stand clear during the heated exchange.The incident also brought back the tension between the two contestants, with Qazi once again using the particular word that Kanika has previously expressed her dislike for. Kanika has earlier made it evident that she does not appreciate being addressed or spoken about in that manner, making the repeated use of the word another point of contention between the two.After Kanika left the bedroom area to complete her kitchen duties, Qazi was seen taking everyone into confidence that he had sorted things with Kanika in the past and explained that the joke was not offensive. He even stated that Kanika had agreed to him and even apologised for misunderstanding the situation. He was seen justifying his comment to the housemates, he said, "Now I became the character of Koi Mil Gaya ka Hrithik Roshan jo akal se baccha hai. I became that character. Kids like lollipop... Chocolates they like.”As soon as other housemates informed Kanika about this, she confronted Qazi. She did not let the comment slide and chose to directly address Qazi. She questioned about the manner in which he was speaking to her.She said, "Maine aapko bola hai na mujhe ye nahi pasand." When Qazi replied that Lollipop is not an offensive word, Kanika made it clear that maybe it is not for him but a lot of people use the word with double meaning and wrong intentions. She added, "Aapko lag raha hai aap isko coverup kar paa rahe ho, but aapka intention nahi tha pure. Aapne bahot smartly khela, Pehle aapne kaha biology padehnge, wahin par aapka intention flip dikh raha tha. Phir aapne immediately bola lollipop. Ab biology mein lollipop kahan se aagaya. Main kal paida nahi hui hoon, na main 4 saal ki bacchi hoon, jisko aap pagal banake nikal jaaoge."When Qazi tried to again talk about intentions, she hit back and asked why did he make such a big issue about Rhiti using a slang in the diss battle. "Phir toh aapka nazariya hai ke aapne Rhiti ke slag marwale shabdh ka galat matlab liya. Woh bhi bol sakti thi na Rhiti. Toh log aise samjhte hain iss shabdh ko. aise he log iss shabh ko bhi samajhte hain."The latest confrontation adds another chapter to Kanika and Qazi’s equation in the Bigg Boss 20 house. articles.title: Mario Lopez reacts to Tiffani Thiessen saying “Saved by the Bell” cast’s residuals are ‘negative’ now
articles.summary: Being a teen idol doesn’t always pay the bills.
articles.body:
Mario Lopez affirmed his Saved by the Bell costar Tiffani Thiessen's claim that they make "negative" money from their residual checks.

Thiessen previously shared how she didn't start "making real money" until she was on Beverly Hills, 90210.

Their costar Mark-Paul Gosselaar once shared that the cast signed "bad deals."

Mario Lopez can attest to his Saved by the Bell costar Tiffani Thiessen 's measly residual checks.

After Thiessen's joked that her kickbacks for the teen sitcom, which ran from 1989 to 1993, were basically nonexistent, Lopez took to X to back up her claim.

Indeed, Thiessen recently got candid about how much money she made for her most iconic TV roles. While her stint as bad girl Valerie Malone on Beverly Hills, 90210 is when she started "making real money," she admitted that her time as girl-next-door Kelly Kapowski on Saved by the Bell earned her very little.

"We made nothing and we just did our job," she said in an interview with SiriusXM's Page Six Radio .

And Saved by the Bell doesn't make her much to this day. In fact, she doesn't think that she receives residual checks for her work on the show at this point.

"I think it has dried out," Thiessen said. "It's like, negative now. It costs more to print the check."

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

It's no secret that the stars of the show, which included Thiessen, Lopez, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Elizabeth Berkley, Lark Voorhies, the late Dennis Haskins, and the late Dustin Diamond, made low salaries. In fact, a recent episode of the docuseries Hollywood Demons shed light on how much Lopez actually made per episode , which was far less than one would expect given the success of the show.

"Mario Lopez said he started out making about $1500 an episode," Denise Simon, a child star manager, said during the episode touching on the struggles of Saved by the Bell' s cast. "That's a lot of money to a kid. But after a second season, in 1991, Saved by the Bell was pulling in roughly $15 million in advertising."

Meanwhile, Gosselaar previously explained that the cast "made really bad deals."

"Poor deals, back then," he said on Watch What Happens Live in 2019 . " It is what it is. You move on, you learn. Great experience."
